MST groups VLANs into several instances.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)?

options.text: prevents routing loops on a router
allows Cisco devices to exchange routing table updates

questions.original: The Spanning-Tree Protocol (STP) creates one path through a switch network in order to prevent Layer 2 loops.

explain.s: STP's job is to **prevent Layer 2 loops**, and the broadcast storms and MAC table instability they cause, by keeping exactly one active path.
x: Routing loops are handled by routing protocols, not STP.
Collision and broadcast domains are set by switches, routers and VLANs.

questions.question: What is the value used to determine which port on a non-root bridge will become a root port in a STP network?

options.text: the highest MAC address of all the ports in the switch
the lowest MAC address of all the ports in the switch

questions.original: STP establishes one root port on each non-root bridge. The root port is the lowest-cost path from the non-root bridge to the root bridge, indicating the direction of the best path to the root bridge. This is primarily based on the path cost to the root bridge.

explain.s: The root port is chosen by the **lowest root path cost**. Ties are broken by the lowest sender bridge ID, then the lowest port ID.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which switch will be the root bridge after the election process is complete?
questions.original: The root bridge is determined by the lowest bridge ID, which consists of the priority value and the MAC address. Because the priority values of all of the switches are identical, the MAC address is used to determine the root bridge. Because S2 has the lowest MAC address, S2 becomes the root bridge.

explain.s: All priorities are equal, so the **lowest MAC address** decides. **S2** has the lowest MAC, so it becomes the root bridge.

questions.question: What are two drawbacks to turning spanning tree off and having multiple paths through the Layer 2 switch network? (Choose two.)

options.text: The MAC address table becomes unstable.
The switch acts like a hub.
Port security shuts down all of the ports that have attached devices.

questions.original: Spanning tree should never be disabled. Without it, the MAC address table becomes unstable, broadcast storms can render network clients and the switches unusable, and multiple copies of unicast frames can be delivered to the end devices.

explain.s: Without STP, redundant links cause loops: **broadcasts circulate forever** (a broadcast storm), and the same MAC is seen on different ports, so the **MAC table keeps changing**. Hosts can also receive duplicate unicast frames.

questions.question: A small company network has six interconnected Layer 2 switches. Currently all switches are using the default bridge priority value. Which value can be used to configure the bridge priority of one of the switches to ensure that it becomes the root bridge in this design?
questions.original: The default bridge priority value for all Cisco switches is 32768. The range is 0 to 61440 in increments of 4096. Thus, the values 1 and 34816 are invalid. Configuring one switch with the lower value of 28672 (and leaving the bridge priority value of all other switches unchanged) will make the switch become the root bridge.

explain.s: Priority must be a **multiple of 4096** from 0 to 61440. The default is 32768. Setting one switch **lower**, such as **28672**, makes it the root.
x: 1 and 34816 aren't multiples of 4096.
32768 is the default and would only tie.
61440 makes it the *least* likely root.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. The administrator tried to create an EtherChannel between S1 and the other two switches via the commands that are shown, but was unsuccessful. What is the problem?

options.text: Traffic cannot be sent to two different switches through the same EtherChannel link.
Traffic cannot be sent to two different switches, but only to two different devices like an EtherChannel-enabled server and a switch.​
Traffic can only be sent to two different switches if EtherChannel is implemented on Gigabit Ethernet interfaces.​
Traffic can only be sent to two different switches if EtherChannel is implemented on Layer 3 switches.​

questions.original: An EtherChannel link can only be created between two switches or between an EtherChannel-enabled server and a switch. Traffic cannot be sent to two different switches through the same EtherChannel link.

explain.s: One EtherChannel must connect the **same two devices**: switch to switch, or switch to an EtherChannel-capable server. You can't bundle links that go to two different switches.
x: Splitting one bundle across two chassis needs special stacking/multichassis features, which are outside this course.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the use of PAgP to create EtherChannels?

options.text: It increases the number of ports that are participating in spanning tree.
It requires more physical links than LACP does.
It mandates that an even number of ports (2, 4, 6, etc.) be used for aggregation.

questions.original: PAgP is used to automatically aggregate multiple ports into an EtherChannel bundle, but it only works between Cisco devices. LACP can be used for the same purpose between Cisco and non-Cisco devices. PAgP must have the same duplex mode at both ends and can use two ports or more. The number of ports depends on the switch platform or module. An EtherChannel aggregated link is seen as one port by the spanning-tree algorithm.

explain.s: **PAgP is Cisco-proprietary**. **LACP (IEEE 802.3ad)** is the open standard and works with other vendors.
x: PAgP doesn't require an even number of links or more links than LACP.
The bundle counts as one STP port, so fewer STP ports, not more.

questions.question: What are two requirements to be able to configure an EtherChannel between two switches? (Choose two.)

options.text: All the interfaces need to work at the same speed.
All interfaces need to be assigned to different VLANs.
Different allowed ranges of VLANs must exist on each end.
All the interfaces need to be working in the same duplex mode.
The interfaces that are involved need to be contiguous on the switch.

questions.original: All interfaces in the EtherChannel bundle must be assigned to the same VLAN or be configured as a trunk. If the allowed range of VLANs is not the same, the interfaces do not form an EtherChannel even when set to auto or desirable mode.

explain.s: Ports in a bundle must match on **speed**, **duplex** and **VLAN settings** (the same access VLAN, or trunk mode with the same allowed VLANs and native VLAN).
x: The ports don't have to be next to each other on the switch.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. On the basis of the output that is shown, what can be determined about the EtherChannel bundle?

options.text: Two Gigabit Ethernet ports are used to form the EtherChannel.
A Cisco proprietary protocol was used to negotiate the EtherChannel link.
The EtherChannel bundle is operating at both Layer 2 and Layer 3.

questions.original: Two protocols can be used to send negotiation frames that are used to try to establish an EtherChannel link: PAgP and LACP. PAgP is Cisco proprietary, and LACP adheres to the industry standard.

explain.s: The output shows the bundle was negotiated with **PAgP**, the **Cisco-proprietary** protocol. LACP is the open-standard alternative.

questions.question: Which two parameters must match on the ports of two switches to create a PAgP EtherChannel between the switches? (Choose two.)
questions.original: For an EtherChannel to be created, the ports that are concerned on the two switches must match in terms of the speed, duplex, and VLAN information. The PAgP mode must be compatible but not necessarily equal. The port ID and the MAC addresses do not have to match.

explain.s: PAgP bundles form only when the ports match on **speed/duplex** and **VLAN information**. The PAgP modes only need to be compatible (desirable/auto), not identical.
x: Port IDs and MAC addresses are always different and don't need to match.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is configuring an EtherChannel link between two switches, SW1 and SW2. Which statement describes the effect after the commands are issued on SW1 and SW2?

options.text: The EtherChannel is established after SW2 initiates the link request.
The EtherChannel is established after SW1 initiates the link request.
The EtherChannel is established without negotiation.

questions.original: The interfaces GigabitEthernet 0/1 and GigabitEthernet 0/2 are configured "on" for the EtherChannel link. This mode forces the interface to channel without PAgP or LACP. The EtherChannel will be established only if the other side is also set to "on". However, the mode on SW2 side is set to PAgP desirable. Thus the EtherChannel link will not be established.

explain.s: Mode **on** forces a bundle *without* any negotiation protocol, so it only works if the other side is also **on**. SW2 is using PAgP **desirable**, which never gets a reply, so the EtherChannel **fails**.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is configuring an EtherChannel link between two switches, SW1 and SW2. However, the EtherChannel link fails to establish. What change in configuration would correct the problem?

options.text: Configure SW2 EtherChannel mode to desirable.
Configure SW2 EtherChannel mode to on.
Configure SW1 EtherChannel mode to on.
Configure SW2 EtherChannel mode to auto.

questions.original: The EtherChannel mode must be compatible on each side for the link to work. The three modes from PAgP protocol are on, desirable, and auto. The three modes from LACP protocol are on, active, and passive. The compatible modes include on-on, auto-desirable, desirable-desirable, active-passive, and active-active. Any other combinations will not form an EtherChannel link.

explain.s: Compatible pairs: PAgP **desirable–desirable** or **desirable–auto**; LACP **active–active** or **active–passive**; **on–on**. SW1 is in **auto**, so SW2 must be **desirable**.

questions.question: A network administrator configured an EtherChannel link with three interfaces between two switches. What is the result if one of the three interfaces is down?

options.text: The remaining two interfaces continue to load balance traffic.
The remaining two interfaces become separate links between the two switches.
One interface becomes an active link for data traffic and the other becomes a backup link.

questions.original: EtherChannel creates an aggregation that is seen as one logical link. It provides redundancy because the overall link is one logical connection. The loss of one physical link within the channel does not create a change in the topology; the EtherChannel remains functional.

explain.s: An EtherChannel is one logical link. If one member fails, the **others keep carrying traffic** (load-balanced), and STP doesn't recalculate.

questions.question: A network administrator is configuring an EtherChannel link between switches SW1 and SW2 by using the command SW1(config-if-range)# channel-group 1 mode auto. Which command must be used on SW2 to enable this EtherChannel?
questions.original:
The possible combinations to establish an EtherChannel between SW1 and SW2 using LACP or PAgP are as follows:
PAgP
on on
auto desirable
desirable desirable
LACP
on on
active active
passive active
The EtherChannel mode chosen on each side of the EtherChannel must be compatible in order to enable it.

explain.s: **auto** (PAgP) only responds; it never starts negotiation. The other side must actively ask, which is **desirable**.
x: active and passive are LACP modes and don't talk to PAgP.

questions.question: Which technology is an open protocol standard that allows switches to automatically bundle physical ports into a single logical link?
questions.original: LACP, or Link Aggregation Control Protocol, is defined by IEEE 802.3ad and is an open standard protocol. LACP allows switches to automatically bundle switch ports into a single logical link to increase bandwidth. PAgP, or Port Aggregation Protocol, performs a similar function, but it is a Cisco proprietary protocol. DTP is Dynamic Trunking Protocol and is used to automatically and dynamically build trunks between switches. Multilink PPP is used to load-balance PPP traffic across multiple serial interfaces.

explain.s: **LACP** (IEEE 802.3ad) is the **open-standard** way to bundle ports into one logical link.
x: PAgP is Cisco-proprietary.
DTP negotiates trunks.
Multilink PPP bundles serial links.

questions.question: What is a requirement to configure a trunking EtherChannel between two switches?

options.text: The allowed range of VLANs must be the same on both switches.
The participating interfaces must be assigned the same VLAN number on both switches.
The participating interfaces must be physically contiguous on a switch.
The participating interfaces must be on the same module on a switch.

questions.original: To enable a trunking EtherChannel successfully, the range of VLANs allowed on all the interfaces must match; otherwise, the EtherChannel cannot be formed. The interfaces involved in an EtherChannel do not have to be physically contiguous, or on the same module. Because the EtherChannel is a trunking one, participating interfaces are configured as trunk mode, not access mode.

explain.s: For a trunking EtherChannel, **all member ports must allow the same VLANs** (and use the same native VLAN). Otherwise the bundle won't form.
x: Ports don't need to be contiguous or on the same module.
Trunk ports don't get an access VLAN number.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using LACP? (Choose two.)

options.text: It allows directly connected switches to negotiate an EtherChannel link.
It eliminates the need for configuring trunk interfaces when deploying VLANs on multiple switches.
It decreases the amount of configuration that is needed on a switch.
It provides a simulated environment for testing link aggregation.
It allows the use of multivendor devices.
LACP allows Fast Ethernet and Gigabit Ethernet interfaces to be mixed within a single EtherChannel.

questions.original: The Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) allows directly connected multivendor switches to negotiate an EtherChannel link. LACP helps create the EtherChannel link by detecting the configuration of each side and making sure that they are compatible so that the EtherChannel link can be enabled when needed.

explain.s: LACP **negotiates** the bundle between directly connected switches, so mismatches are caught. Because it's an open standard, it also works with **other vendors' devices**.
x: You can't mix Fast Ethernet and Gigabit ports in one bundle.

questions.question: A switch is configured to run STP. What term describes a non-root port that is permitted to forward traffic on the network?

explain.s: A **designated port** is the best port on a segment toward the root. It isn't the switch's root port, but it **forwards traffic**. (All ports on the root bridge are designated.)

questions.question: What are two advantages of EtherChannel? (Choose two.)

options.text: Spanning Tree Protocol views the physical links in an EtherChannel as one logical connection.
Load balancing occurs between links configured as different EtherChannels.
Configuring the EtherChannel interface provides consistency in the configuration of the physical links.
Spanning Tree Protocol ensures redundancy by transitioning failed interfaces in an EtherChannel to a forwarding state.
EtherChannel uses upgraded physical links to provide increased bandwidth.

questions.original: EtherChannel configuration of one logical interface ensures configuration consistency across the physical links in the EtherChannel. The EtherChannel provides increased bandwidth using existing switch ports without requiring any upgrades to the physical interfaces. Load balancing methods are implemented between links that are part of the same Etherchannel. Because EtherChannel views the bundled physical links as one logical connection, spanning tree recalculation is not required if one of the bundled physical links fail. If a physical interface fails, STP cannot transition the failed interface into a forwarding state.

explain.s: EtherChannel treats the bundle as **one logical link**, so STP doesn't block members. You also configure **one port-channel interface**, which keeps every member configured consistently.
x: Load balancing happens inside one bundle, not between bundles.
It uses existing ports; no upgraded links are needed.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. What are the possible port roles for ports A, B, C, and D in this RSTP-enabled network?
questions.original: Because S1 is the root bridge, B is a designated port, and C and D root ports. RSTP supports a new port type, alternate port in discarding state, that can be port A in this scenario.

explain.s: S1 is the root, so its port **B is designated**. **C and D** are the best paths to the root on their switches, so they're **root ports**. **A** is a redundant path in RSTP's **alternate** role, which is discarding.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which switching technology would allow each access layer switch link to be aggregated to provide more bandwidth between each Layer 2 switch and the Layer 3 switch?
questions.original: PortFast is used to reduce the amount of time that a port spends going through the spanning-tree algorithm, so that devices can start sending data sooner. Trunking can be implemented in conjunction with EtherChannel, but trunking alone does not aggregate switch links. HSRP is used to load-balance traffic across two different connections to Layer 3 devices for default gateway redundancy. HSRP does not aggregate links at either Layer 2 or Layer 3 as EtherChannel does.

explain.s: **EtherChannel** bundles several physical uplinks into one logical link for more bandwidth, and STP doesn't block any of them.
x: Trunking carries VLANs but doesn't add bandwidth.
HSRP provides gateway redundancy.
PortFast speeds up edge ports.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. An administrator wants to form an EtherChannel between the two switches by using the Port Aggregation Protocol. If switch S1 is configured to be in auto mode, which mode should be configured on S2 to form the EtherChannel?
questions.original: An EtherChannel will be formed via PAgP when both switches are in on mode or when one of them is in auto or desirable mode and the other is in desirable mode.

explain.s: PAgP **auto** waits to be asked, so S2 must be **desirable** to start the negotiation.

questions.question: Open the PT Activity. Perform the tasks in the activity instructions and then answer the question.

stem.text: Which set of configuration commands issued on SW1 will successfully complete the EtherChannel link between SW1 and SW2?

questions.original: Issuing the show running-configuration command on SW1 shows that interface GigabitEthernet0/1 is missing the channel-group 1 mode desirable command which will compete the EtherChannel configuration for interface GigabitEthernet0/1 and interface GigabitEthernet0/2.

explain.s: On SW1, Gi0/2 is already in channel-group 1, but **Gi0/1 is missing** from it. Add Gi0/1 to the same group with a compatible mode.

questions.question: A set of switches is being connected in a LAN topology. Which STP bridge priority value will make it least likely for the switch to be selected as the root?
questions.original: The STP bridge priority is a two byte number, but it can only be customized in increments of 4096. The smaller number is preferred, but the largest usable priority value is 61440.

explain.s: Priority goes in steps of 4096, and **lower is better**. The **highest valid value, 61440**, makes a switch the *least* likely root.
x: 65535 isn't a valid priority.

questions.question: In which two PVST+ port states are MAC addresses learned? (Choose two.)
questions.original: The two PVST+ port states during which MAC addresses are learned and populate the MAC address table are the learning and the forwarding states.

explain.s: PVST+ learns MAC addresses in the **learning** and **forwarding** states. Blocking and listening only process BPDUs.

questions.question: Which port role is assigned to the switch port that has the lowest cost to reach the root bridge?
questions.original: The root port on a switch is the port with the lowest cost to reach the root bridge.

explain.s: The **root port** is the switch's port with the **lowest cost to the root bridge**. Every non-root switch has exactly one.

questions.question: A switch is configured to run STP. What term describes the switch port closest, in terms of overall cost, to the root bridge?

explain.s: The **root port** is the port closest to the root bridge by total path cost.

questions.question: A switch is configured to run STP. What term describes a field used to specify a VLAN ID?

explain.s: The **extended system ID** is the 12-bit part of the bridge ID that holds the **VLAN ID**.

questions.question: A switch is configured to run STP. What term describes the reference point for all path calculations?

explain.s: Every STP path cost is measured **to the root bridge**. It is the reference point of the tree.

questions.question: A switch is configured to run STP. What term describes a field that has a default value of 32,768 and is the initial deciding factor when electing a root bridge?

explain.s: **Bridge priority** (default **32768**) is compared first in the root election. The MAC address breaks ties.

questions.question: Which statement describes an EtherChannel implementation?

options.text: PAgP cannot be used in conjunction with EtherChannel.
A trunked port can be part of an EtherChannel bundle.
EtherChannel can support up to a maximum of ten separate links.

questions.original: Up to 16 links can be grouped in an EtherChannel by using the the PAgP or LACP protocol. EtherChannel can be configured as a Layer 2 bundle or a Layer 3 bundle. Configuring a Layer 3 bundle is beyond the scope of this course. If a trunked port is a part of the EtherChannel bundle, all ports in the bundle need to be trunk ports and the native VLAN must be the same on all of these ports. A best practice is to apply the configuration to the port channel interface. The configuration is then automatically applied to the individual ports.

explain.s: **Trunk ports can be bundled**. All members then have to be trunks with the same allowed VLANs and native VLAN.
x: EtherChannel can be Layer 2 or Layer 3.
PAgP is one of its negotiation protocols.
Up to 8 active links (16 with LACP standby), not 10.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator issued the show etherchannel summary command on the switch S1. What conclusion can be drawn?

options.text: The port aggregation protocol PAgP is misconfigured.
FastEthernet ports Fa0/1, Fa0/2, and Fa0/3 do not join the EtherChannel.

questions.original: The EtherChannel status shows as (SD), which means it is a Layer 2 EtherChannel with a status of D or down. Because the EtherChannel is down, the status of the interfaces in the channel group is stand-alone. PAgP is configured on S1, but there is no indication whether it is configured correctly on S1. The problem might also be the adjacent switch EtherChannel configuration.

explain.s: In `show etherchannel summary`, **(SD)** means a Layer 2 port-channel (S) that is **down** (D). The members show as stand-alone, so **the EtherChannel is not working**.

questions.question: Which statement describes a characteristic of EtherChannel?

options.text: It can combine up to a maximum of 4 physical links.
It can bundle mixed types of 100 Mb/s and 1Gb/s Ethernet links.
It consists of multiple parallel links between a switch and a router.
It is made by combining multiple physical links that are seen as one link between two switches.

questions.original: An EtherChannel is formed by combining multiple (same type) Ethernet physical links so they are seen and configured as one logical link. It provides an aggregated link between two switches. Currently each EtherChannel can consist of up to eight compatibly configured Ethernet ports.

explain.s: EtherChannel bundles **several identical physical links into one logical link** between two switches (or a switch and a server).
x: You can't mix speeds.
Up to 8 active links, not 4.

questions.question: Which two channel group modes would place an interface in a negotiating state using PAgP? (Choose two.)
questions.original: There are three modes available when configuring an interface for PAgP: on, desirable, and auto. Only desirable and auto place the interface in a negotiating state. The active and passive states are used to configure LACP and not PAgP.

explain.s: PAgP modes **desirable** (actively negotiates) and **auto** (responds) both negotiate. **on** forces the channel with no negotiation. active and passive belong to LACP.

questions.question: Which mode configuration setting would allow formation of an EtherChannel link between switches SW1 and SW2 without sending negotiation traffic?

options.text:
SW1: auto
SW2: auto
trunking enabled on both switches

SW1: auto
SW2: auto
PortFast enabled on both switches

questions.original: The auto channel-group keyword enables PAgP only if a PAgP device is detected on the opposite side of the link. If the auto keyword is used, the only way to form an EtherChannel link is if the opposite connected device is configured with the desirable keyword. PortFast and trunking technologies are irrelevant to forming an EtherChannel link. Even though an EtherChannel can be formed if both sides are configured in desirable mode, PAgP is active and PAgP messages are being sent constantly across the link, decreasing the amount of bandwidth available for user traffic.

explain.s: Mode **on** on both ends forms the EtherChannel **without sending PAgP or LACP packets**.
x: desirable and active/passive send negotiation traffic.
auto–auto never forms a channel.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. An EtherChannel was configured between switches S1 and S2, but the interfaces do not form an EtherChannel. What is the problem?

options.text: The interface port-channel number has to be different on each switch.
The switch ports were not configured with speed and duplex mode.
The switch ports have to be configured as access ports with each port having a VLAN assigned.​
The EtherChannel was not configured with the same allowed range of VLANs on each interface.

explain.s: The member trunks on S1 and S2 allow **different VLAN ranges**. Every member must have the same allowed VLAN list, or the bundle won't form.

questions.question: When EtherChannel is configured, which mode will force an interface into a port channel without exchanging aggregation protocol packets?
questions.original: For both LACP and PAgP, the "on" mode will force an interface into an EtherChannel without exchanging protocol packets.

explain.s: **on** forces the port into the channel **without exchanging PAgP or LACP packets**.

questions.question: What are two load-balancing methods in the EtherChannel technology? (Choose two.)

options.text: combination of source port and IP to destination port and IP
combination of source MAC and IP to destination MAC and IP

questions.original: Depending on the hardware platform, one or more load-balancing methods can be implemented. These methods include source MAC to destination MAC load balancing or source IP to destination IP load balancing, across the physical links.

explain.s: EtherChannel can load-balance by **source/destination MAC** or **source/destination IP** (and, on some platforms, by port numbers). The method is set with `port-channel load-balance`.

questions.question: Which protocol provides up to 16 instances of RSTP, combines many VLANs with the same physical and logical topology into a common RSTP instance, and provides support for PortFast, BPDU guard, BPDU filter, root guard, and loop guard?
questions.original: MST is the Cisco implementation of MSTP, an IEEE standard protocol that provides up to 16 instances of RSTP and combines many VLANs with the same physical and logical topology into a common RSTP instance. Each instance supports PortFast, BPDU guard, BPDU filter, root guard, and loop guard. STP and RSTP assume only one spanning-tree instance for the entire bridged network, regardless of the number of VLANs. PVST+ provides a separate 802.1D spanning-tree instance for each VLAN that is configured in the network.

explain.s: **MST** maps many VLANs into a few **RSTP instances** (up to 16 in Cisco's implementation), and it supports PortFast, BPDU guard, root guard and so on.

questions.question: What is the outcome of a Layer 2 broadcast storm?

options.text: Routers will take over the forwarding of frames as switches become congested.
New traffic is discarded by the switch because it is unable to be processed.
CSMA/CD will cause each host to continue transmitting frames.
ARP broadcast requests are returned to the transmitting host.

questions.original: When the network is saturated with broadcast traffic that is looping between switches, new traffic is discarded by each switch because it is unable to be processed.

explain.s: In a broadcast storm, looping broadcasts use up all the bandwidth and CPU. The switches can't keep up, so **new traffic is dropped**.

questions.question: Which two network design features require Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) to ensure correct network operation? (Choose two.)

options.text: link-state dynamic routing that provides redundant routes
removing single points of failure with multiple Layer 2 switches

questions.original: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is required to ensure correct network operation when designing a network with multiple interconnected Layer 2 switches or using redundant links to eliminate single points of failure between Layer 2 switches. Routing is a Layer 3 function and does not relate to STP. VLANs do reduce the number of broadcast domains but relate to Layer 3 subnets, not STP.

explain.s: STP is needed whenever there are **redundant Layer 2 links** or **multiple switches added to remove single points of failure**, because both create loops.
x: Static and dynamic routing are Layer 3.
VLANs limit broadcasts but don't stop loops.

questions.question: A network administrator has configured an EtherChannel between two switches that are connected via four trunk links. If the physical interface for one of the trunk links changes to a down state, what happens to the EtherChannel?

options.text: Spanning Tree Protocol will transition the failed physical interface into forwarding mode.
Spanning Tree Protocol will recalculate the remaining trunk links.
The EtherChannel will transition to a down state.

questions.original: EtherChannel offers redundancy by bundling multiple trunk links into one logical connection. Failure of one physical link within the EtherChannel will not create a change in the topology and therefore a recalculation by Spanning Tree is unnecessary. Just one physical link must remain operational for the EtherChannel to continue to function.

explain.s: If one member of a 4-link EtherChannel goes down, **the EtherChannel stays up** on the remaining links. STP still sees one logical link, so it doesn't recalculate.

questions.question: A DHCP-enabled client PC has just booted. During which two steps will the client PC use broadcast messages when communicating with a DHCP server? (Choose two.)
questions.original: All DHCP messages between a DHCP-enabled client and a DHCP server are using broadcast messages until after the DHCPACK message. The DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST messages are the only messages that are sent by a DHCP-enabled client. All DHCP messages between a DHCP-enabled client and a DHCP server use broadcast messages when the client is obtaining a lease for the first time.

explain.s: A client getting its first lease sends two messages, and both are **broadcasts**: **DHCPDISCOVER** (it doesn't know any server yet) and **DHCPREQUEST** (accepting one offer, which also tells the other servers they weren't chosen).
x: DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK and DHCPNAK come from the server, not the client.

questions.question: An administrator issues the commands:

stem.text:
Router(config)# interface g0/1
Router(config-if)# ip address dhcp
What is the administrator trying to achieve?

options.text: configuring the router to act as a DHCPv4 server
configuring the router to obtain IP parameters from a DHCPv4 server
configuring the router to act as a relay agent
configuring the router to resolve IP address conflicts

explain.s: `ip address dhcp` makes the router interface a **DHCPv4 client**: it gets its IP settings from a DHCP server, such as the ISP's.
x: A DHCP server is configured with `ip dhcp pool`.
A relay agent uses `ip helper-address`.

questions.question: When a client is requesting an initial address lease from a DHCP server, why is the DHCPREQUEST message sent as a broadcast?

options.text: The client does not yet know the IP address of the DHCP server that sent the offer.
The DHCP server may be on a different subnet, so the request must be sent as a broadcast.
The client does not have a MAC address assigned yet, so it cannot send a unicast message at Layer 2.
The client may have received offers from multiple servers, and the broadcast serves to implicitly decline those other offers.

questions.original: During the initial DHCP exchange between a client and server, the client broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER message looking for DHCP servers. Multiple servers may be configured to respond to this request with DHCPOFFER messages. The client will choose the lease from one of the servers by sending a DHCPREQUEST message. It sends this message as a broadcast so that the other DHCP servers that sent offers will know that their offers were declined and the corresponding address can go back into the pool.

explain.s: Several servers may have sent offers. Broadcasting the **DHCPREQUEST** tells the chosen server *yes* and the others *no*, so they can return their offered addresses to the pool.

questions.question: Which DHCP IPv4 message contains the following information?

stem.text:
Destination address: 255.255.255.255
Client IPv4 address: 0.0.0.0
Default gateway address: 0.0.0.0
Subnet mask: 0.0.0.0

explain.s: Destination 255.255.255.255 and **all zeros for the client's own settings** means the client has no IP information yet. It's the very first message: **DHCPDISCOVER**.

questions.question: Place the options in the following order:

options.text: a client initiating a message to find a DHCP server - DHCPDISCOVER
a DHCP server responding to the initial request by a client - DHCPOFFER
the client accepting the IP address provided by the DHCP server - DHCPREQUEST
the DHCP server confirming that the lease has been accepted - DHCPACK

explain.s:
DHCPv4 order (**DORA**):
1. **DHCPDISCOVER** – the client looks for a server.
2. **DHCPOFFER** – the server offers an address.
3. **DHCPREQUEST** – the client accepts it.
4. **DHCPACK** – the server confirms the lease.

questions.question: Which protocol automates assignment of IP addresses on a network, and which port number does it use? (Choose two.)
questions.original: DNS uses port 53 and translates URLs to IP addresses. SMB provides shared access to files and printers and uses port 445. Port 80 is used by HTTP. HTTP is a protocol used to communicate between a web browser and a server.

explain.s: **DHCP** assigns IP settings automatically. DHCPv4 servers listen on **UDP 67**, and clients use UDP 68.
x: DNS uses port 53.
SMB uses 445.
HTTP uses 80.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. PC1 is configured to obtain a dynamic IP address from the DHCP server. PC1 has been shut down for two weeks. When PC1 boots and tries to request an available IP address, which destination IP address will PC1 place in the IP header?
questions.original: When a host boots and has been configured for dynamic IP addressing, the device tries to obtain a valid IP address. It sends a DHCPDISCOVER message. This is a broadcast message because the DHCP server address is unknown (by design). The destination IP address in the IP header is 255.255.255.255 and the destination MAC address is FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF.

explain.s: After two weeks the lease has expired, so PC1 starts over with a **DHCPDISCOVER** broadcast. The destination IP is **255.255.255.255** and the destination MAC is FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF.

questions.question: Which message does an IPv4 host use to reply when it receives a DHCPOFFER message from a DHCP server?
questions.original: When the client receives the DHCPOFFER from the server, it sends back a DHCPREQUEST broadcast message. On receiving the DHCPREQUEST message, the server replies with a unicast DHCPACK message.

explain.s: The client answers an offer with **DHCPREQUEST**, and the server then confirms with **DHCPACK**.

questions.question: Which command, when issued in the interface configuration mode of a router, enables the interface to acquire an IPv4 address automatically from an ISP, when that link to the ISP is enabled?
questions.original: The ip address dhcp interface configuration command configures an Ethernet interface as a DHCP client. The service dhcp global configuration command enables the DHCPv4 server process on the router. The ip helper-address command is issued to enable DHCP relay on the router. The ip dhcp pool command creates the name of a pool of addresses that the server can assign to hosts.

explain.s: `ip address dhcp` makes the interface a DHCP client, so it gets its address from the ISP.
x: `service dhcp` enables the DHCP server and relay service.
`ip helper-address` sets up relaying.
`ip dhcp pool` creates a server pool.

questions.question: Which kind of message is sent by a DHCP client when its IP address lease has expired?​
questions.original: When the IP address lease time of the DHCP client expires, it sends a DHCPREQUEST unicast message directly to the DHCPv4 server that originally offered the IPv4 address.

explain.s: To renew, a client sends a **unicast DHCPREQUEST** straight to the server that gave it the lease. (That's the answer the course expects.)
explain.note: Strictly speaking, the client renews *before* the lease runs out (at 50% of the lease time). If a lease has fully expired, the client starts over with a broadcast DHCPDISCOVER, as in another question in this set.

questions.question: A host PC is attempting to lease an address through DHCP. What message is sent by the server to let the client know it is able to use the provided IP information?
questions.original: When a host uses DHCP to automatically configure an IP address, the typically sends two messages: the DHCPDISCOVER message and the DHCPREQUEST message. These two messages are usually sent as broadcasts to ensure that all DHCP servers receive them. The servers respond to these messages using DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK, and DHCPNACK messages, depending on the circumstance.

explain.s: **DHCPACK** is the server's final confirmation: *the lease is yours, go ahead and use it*. (DHCPNAK would mean the offer is no longer valid.)

questions.question: What is one indication that a Windows computer did not receive an IPv4 address from a DHCP server?

options.text: The computer receives an IP address that starts with 169.254.
Windows displays a DHCP timeout message.
The computer cannot ping other devices on the same network with IP addresses in the 169.254.0.0/16 range.

questions.original: When a Windows PC cannot communicate with an IPv4 DHCP server, the computer automatically assigns an IP address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range. Any other device on the same network that receives an address in the same range is reachable.​

explain.s: If Windows can't reach a DHCP server, it gives itself an **APIPA** address from **169.254.0.0/16**. Seeing 169.254.x.x is the classic sign that DHCP failed.

questions.question: Which DHCPv4 message will a client send to accept an IPv4 address that is offered by a DHCP server?
questions.original: When a DHCP client receives DHCPOFFER messages, it will send a broadcast DHCPREQUEST message for two purposes. First, it indicates to the offering DHCP server that it would like to accept the offer and bind the IP address. Second, it notifies any other responding DHCP servers that their offers are declined.

explain.s: To accept an offer, the client sends a **broadcast DHCPREQUEST**. The broadcast accepts the chosen offer and quietly turns down any others.

questions.question: A small coffee shop is offering free Wi-Fi to customers. The network includes a wireless router and a DSL modem that is connected to the local phone company. What method is typically used to configure the connection to the phone company?

options.text: Set the WAN connection in the wireless router as a DHCP client.
Set the connection between the wireless router and the DSL modem as a private IP network.
Set the DSL modem as a DHCP client to get a public IP address from the wireless router.
Set the DSL modem as a DHCP client to the phone company and a DHCP server for the internal connection.

questions.original: In a SOHO environment, a wireless router connects to an ISP via a DSL or cable modem. The IP address between the wireless router and ISP site is typically assigned by the ISP through DHCP. The DSL modem does not manage IP address allocation.

explain.s: At home or in a small office, the wireless router's **WAN port is a DHCP client**: it gets its public address from the ISP. Its LAN side acts as the DHCP server for the customers' devices.

questions.question: A company uses DHCP to manage IP address deployment for employee workstations. The IT department deploys multiple DHCP servers in the data center and uses DHCP relay agents to facilitate the DHCP requests from workstations. Which two UDP ports are used to forward DHCP traffic? (Choose two.)
questions.original: The DHCP protocol operates with 2 UDP ports. UDP port 67 is the destination port for DHCP servers, and DHCP clients use UDP port 68.

explain.s: DHCPv4 uses **UDP 67** (server) and **UDP 68** (client). A relay agent forwards this traffic to the remote server.

questions.question: A client device on an Ethernet segment needs an IP address in order to communicate on the network. A DHCP server with IP address 192.168.1.1 has been configured and enabled on the network. How will a client device obtain a usable IP address for this network?

options.text: Send a DHCPACK packet to the default gateway address.
Use a statically configured IP address from the pool of IP addresses that is offered by the DHCP server.
Send a DHCPDISCOVER message to physical address FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF.
Send a DHCPREQUEST packet to IP address 255.255.255.255.

questions.original: Like IP addressing, there is also a special MAC address for broadcast purposes: FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF. When a DHCP client needs to send a DHCP Discover message in order to seek DHCP servers, the client will use this MAC address as the destination MAC address in the Ethernet frame. It does this because it has no knowledge of the IP and MAC addresses of DHCP servers.

explain.s: The client doesn't know where the server is, so it sends **DHCPDISCOVER** as a broadcast: destination MAC **FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF** and destination IP 255.255.255.255.

questions.question: What is an advantage of configuring a Cisco router as a relay agent?

options.text: It can provide relay services for multiple UDP services.
It reduces the response time from a DHCP server.
It can forward both broadcast and multicast messages on behalf of clients.
It will allow DHCPDISCOVER messages to pass without alteration.

questions.original:
By default, the ip helper-address command forwards the following eight UDP services:
Port 37: Time
Port 49: TACACS
Port 53: DNS
Port 67: DHCP/BOOTP client
Port 68: DHCP/BOOTP server
Port 69: TFTP
Port 137: NetBIOS name service
Port 138: NetBIOS datagram service

explain.s: `ip helper-address` forwards **several UDP broadcast services** by default, not just DHCP: TFTP, DNS, Time, TACACS and NetBIOS too.

questions.question: Which statement is true about DHCP operation?​

options.text: When a device that is configured to use DHCP boots, the client broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER message to identify any available DHCP servers on the network.​
A client must wait for lease expiration before it sends another DHCPREQUEST message.​
If the client receives several DHCPOFFER messages from different servers, it sends a unicast DHCPREQUEST message to the server from which it chooses to obtain the IP information.
The DHCPDISCOVER message contains the IP address and subnet mask to be assigned, the IP address of the DNS server, and the IP address of the default gateway.​

questions.original: The client broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER message to identify any available DHCP servers on the network. A DHCP server replies with a DHCPOFFER message. This message offers to the client a lease that contains such information as the IP address and subnet mask to be assigned, the IP address of the DNS server, and the IP address of the default gateway. After the client receives the lease, the received information must be renewed through another DHCPREQUEST message prior to the lease expiration.

explain.s: A DHCP client starts by **broadcasting DHCPDISCOVER** to find any available server.
x: Renewal happens before the lease expires.
The DHCPREQUEST that accepts an offer is broadcast, not unicast.
The address, mask, DNS and gateway arrive in the OFFER, not the DISCOVER.

questions.question: Order the DHCP message types as they would occur between a DHCP client and a DHCP server.
questions.original:
The DHCPDISCOVER message is used to identify any DHCP servers on a network.
The DHCPOFFER message is used by a server to offer a lease to a client. The DHCPREQUEST message is used to identify both the specific DHCP server and the lease that the client is accepting.
The DHCPACK message is used by a server to finalize a successful lease with a client.
The DHCPNAK message is used when an offered lease is no longer valid.

explain.s: Order: **DHCPDISCOVER → DHCPOFFER → DHCPREQUEST → DHCPACK**. If the lease can't be granted, the server sends DHCPNAK instead of ACK.

questions.question: A network administrator configures a router to send RA messages with M flag as 0 and O flag as 1. Which statement describes the effect of this configuration when a PC tries to configure its IPv6 address?

options.text: It should contact a DHCPv6 server for the prefix, the prefix-length information, and an interface ID that is both random and unique.
It should use the information that is contained in the RA message and contact a DHCPv6 server for additional information.
It should use the information that is contained in the RA message exclusively.
It should contact a DHCPv6 server for all the information that it needs.

questions.original: ICMPv6 RA messages contain two flags to indicate whether a workstation should use SLAAC, a DHCPv6 server, or a combination to configure its IPv6 address. These two flags are M flag and O flag. When both flags are 0 (by default), a client must only use the information in the RA message. When M flag is 0 and O flag is 1, a client should use the information in the RA message and look for the other configuration parameters (such as DNS server addresses) on DHCPv6 servers.

explain.s: RA flags: **M=0, O=1** means **stateless DHCPv6**. The host builds its own address from the RA (SLAAC) and asks a DHCPv6 server only for **other settings**, such as DNS.
x: M=1 is stateful DHCPv6 (the server hands out addresses).
M=0, O=0 is SLAAC only.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. What should be done to allow PC-A to receive an IPv6 address from the DHCPv6 server?

options.text: Add the ipv6 dhcp relay command to interface Fa0/0.
Change the ipv6 nd managed-config-flag command to ipv6 nd other-config-flag.
Configure the ipv6 nd managed-config-flag command on interface Fa0/1.
Add the IPv6 address 2001:DB8:1234:5678::10/64 to the interface configuration of the DHCPv6 server.

questions.original: Client DHCPv6 messages are sent to a multicast address with link-local scope, which means that the messages will not be forwarded by routers. Because the client and server are on different subnets on different interfaces, the message will not reach the server. The router can be configured to relay the DHCPv6 messages from the client to the server by configuring the ipv6 dhcp relay command on the interface that is connected to the client.

explain.s: DHCPv6 client messages go to a **link-local multicast** address, which routers don't forward. Put `ipv6 dhcp relay destination` on the router interface **facing the client** (Fa0/0).

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is implementing the stateless DHCPv6 operation for the company. Clients are configuring IPv6 addresses as expected. However, the clients are not getting the DNS server address and the domain name information configured in the DHCP pool. What could be the cause of the problem?

options.text: The DNS server address is not on the same network as the clients are on.
The router is configured for SLAAC operation.
The GigabitEthernet interface is not activated.
The clients cannot communicate with the DHCPv6 server, evidenced by the number of active clients being 0.

questions.original: The router is configured for SLAAC operation because there is no configuration command to change the RA M and O flag value. By default, both M and O flags are set to 0. In order to permint stateless DHCPv6 operation, the interface command ipv6 nd other-config-flag should be issued. The GigabitEthernet interface is in working condition because clients can get RA messages and configure their IPv6 addresses as expected. Also, the fact that R1 is the DHCPv6 server and clients are getting RA messages indicates that clients can communicate with the DHCP server. The number of active clients is 0 because the DHCPv6 server does not maintain the state of clients IPv6 addresses (it is not configured for stateful DHCPv6 operation). The DNS server address issue is not relevant to the problem.

explain.s: The pool is set up, but the router's RAs still have **O=0**, which is the default SLAAC behavior. Clients therefore never ask the DHCPv6 server for DNS or domain information. Turn on the O flag.

questions.question: Question as presented:

stem.text: A stateless DHCPv6 client would send a DHCPv6 INFORMATION-REQUEST message as step 3 in the process.

explain.s: **True.** Stateless DHCPv6: 1) the client sends an RS, 2) the router replies with an RA (O=1), 3) the client sends an **INFORMATION-REQUEST** to the DHCPv6 server, 4) the server replies with a REPLY containing DNS and other settings.

questions.question: A company uses the SLAAC method to configure IPv6 addresses for the employee workstations. Which address will a client use as its default gateway?​

options.text: the global unicast address of the router interface that is attached to the network
the unique local address of the router interface that is attached to the network
the link-local address of the router interface that is attached to the network

questions.original: When a PC is configured to use the SLAAC method for configuring IPv6 addresses, it will use the prefix and prefix-length information that is contained in the RA message, combined with a 64-bit interface ID (obtained by using the EUI-64 process or by using a random number that is generated by the client operating system), to form an IPv6 address. It uses the link-local address of the router interface that is attached to the LAN segment as its IPv6 default gateway address.

explain.s: IPv6 hosts use the router's **link-local address** (from the RA) as their default gateway, not its global address.
x: The all-routers multicast (ff02::2) is where Router Solicitations are sent; it isn't a gateway.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is configuring a router for DHCPv6 operation. Which conclusion can be drawn based on the commands?

options.text: The router is configured for stateful DHCPv6 operation, but the DHCP pool configuration is incomplete.
The DHCPv6 server name is ACAD_CLASS.
Clients would configure the interface IDs above 0010.
The router is configured for stateless DHCPv6 operation.

questions.original: The DHCPv6 is for the stateless DHCPv6 operation that is indicated by changing the O flag to 1 and leaving the M flag as default, which is 0. Therefore, it is not configured for stateful DHCPv6 operation. Although the DNS server has the interface ID 0010, clients in stateless DHCPv6 operation will configure their interface IDs either by EUI-64 or a random number. The ACAD_CLASS is the name of the DHCP pool, not the DHCP server name.

explain.s: Only the **O flag** is set (`ipv6 nd other-config-flag`) and the pool has just DNS and domain information, so this is **stateless DHCPv6**. ACAD_CLASS is the *pool* name, and clients create their own interface IDs.

questions.question: A network administrator is analyzing the features that are supported by different first-hop router redundancy protocols. Which statement describes a feature that is associated with HSRP?

options.text: HSRP uses active and standby routers.
It allows load balancing between a group of redundant routers.
It uses ICMP messages in order to assign the default gateway to hosts.

questions.original: The HSRP first-hop router redundancy protocol is Cisco proprietary and supports standby and active devices. VRRPv2 and VRRPv3 are nonproprietary. GLBP is Cisco proprietary and supports load balancing between a group of redundant routers.

explain.s: **HSRP** (Cisco) picks one **active** router to forward traffic and one **standby** router ready to take over.
x: It's Cisco-proprietary; VRRP is the open standard.
Load balancing is GLBP.
ICMP-based router discovery is IRDP.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. What protocol can be configured on gateway routers R1 and R2 that will allow traffic from the internal LAN to be load balanced across the two gateways to the Internet?
questions.original: GLBP, or Group Load Balancing Protocol, allows multiple routers to act as a single default gateway for hosts. GLBP load balances the traffic across the individual routers on a per host basis.

explain.s: **GLBP** gives hosts one virtual gateway but **load-balances** them across several routers by handing out different virtual MAC addresses.
x: STP, PVST and PVST+ are Layer 2 loop prevention, not gateway protocols.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network engineer is troubleshooting host connectivity on a LAN that uses a first hop redundancy protocol. Which IPv4 gateway address should be configured on the host?
questions.original: The host default gateway address should be the FHRP (in this case GLBP) virtual IP address.

explain.s: With an FHRP, hosts use the **virtual IP address** as their default gateway, here **192.168.2.100**, not either router's real IP.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which destination MAC address is used when frames are sent from the workstation to the default gateway?

options.text: MAC address of the virtual router
MAC address of the standby router
MAC addresses of both the forwarding and standby routers
MAC address of the forwarding router

questions.original: The IP address of the virtual router acts as the default gateway for all the workstations. Therefore, the MAC address that is returned by the Address Resolution Protocol to the workstation will be the MAC address of the virtual router.

explain.s: The host ARPs for the **virtual IP** and gets the **virtual router's MAC address**, so frames go to that virtual MAC. Whichever router is active answers for it.

questions.question: Question as presented:

stem.text: Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP) is a Cisco-proprietary protocol that is designed to allow for transparent failover of a first-hop IPv4 device.

explain.s: **True.** HSRP is Cisco's FHRP. It lets an active and a standby router share one virtual IP and MAC, so if the active gateway fails, hosts switch over without noticing.

questions.question: Which FHRP implementation is a Cisco-proprietary protocol that suppports IPv4 load sharing?

explain.s: **GLBP** is Cisco-proprietary and **load-shares** IPv4 traffic across several gateways.
x: VRRPv3 is an open standard.
IRDP uses ICMP.
GLBP for IPv6 is the IPv6 version.

questions.question: The address pool of a DHCP server is configured with 10.92.71.0/25. The network administrator reserves 8 IP addresses for servers. How many IP addresses are left in the pool to be assigned to other hosts?
questions.original:
Calculate the maximum number of hosts available for the slash value and subtract the required static IP addresses required for the devices.
/24 = 254 hosts
/25 = 126 hosts
/26 = 62 hosts
/27 = 30 hosts
/28 = 14 hosts

explain.s: A /25 has 2^7 − 2 = **126** usable addresses. Take away the 8 reserved: **126 − 8 = 118**.

questions.question: Question as presented:

stem.text: The broadcast DHCPDISCOVER message finds DHCPv4 servers on the network. When the DHCPv4 server receives a DHCPDISCOVER message, it reserves an available IPv4 address to lease to the client and sends the unicast DHCPOFFER message to the requesting client. When the client receives the DHCPOFFER from the server, it sends back a DHCPREQUEST. On receiving the DHCPREQUEST message the server replies with a unicast DHCPACK message. DHCPREPLY and DHCPINFORMATION-REQUEST are DHCPv6 messages.

explain.s: **DHCPv4 recap:** a broadcast DISCOVER → a unicast OFFER (the server reserves an address) → a REQUEST → a unicast ACK. REPLY and INFORMATION-REQUEST are **DHCPv6** messages, not DHCPv4.

questions.question: After a host has generated an IPv6 address by using the DHCPv6 or SLAAC process, how does the host verify that the address is unique and therefore usable?

options.text: The host sends an ICMPv6 echo request message to the DHCPv6 or SLAAC-learned address and if no reply is returned, the address is considered unique.
The host sends an ICMPv6 neighbor solicitation message to the DHCP or SLAAC-learned address and if no neighbor advertisement is returned, the address is considered unique.
The host checks the local neighbor cache for the learned address and if the address is not cached, it it considered unique.
The host sends an ARP broadcast to the local link and if no hosts send a reply, the address is considered unique.

questions.original: Before a host can actually configure and use an IPv6 address learned through SLAAC or DHCP, the host must verify that no other host is already using that address. To verify that the address is indeed unique, the host sends an ICMPv6 neighbor solicitation to the address. If no neighbor advertisement is returned, the host considers the address to be unique and configures it on the interface.

explain.s: **Duplicate Address Detection (DAD):** the host sends an ICMPv6 **Neighbor Solicitation** for its own new address. If no **Neighbor Advertisement** comes back, nobody else is using it.
x: IPv6 has no ARP; it uses Neighbor Discovery.

questions.question: Which statement describes HSRP?​

options.text: It is used within a group of routers for selecting an active device and a standby device to provide gateway services to a LAN.
It uses ICMP to allow IPv4 hosts to locate routers that provide IPv4 connectivity to remote IP networks.​
If the virtual router master fails, one router is elected as the virtual router master with the other routers acting as backups.
It is an open standard protocol.

questions.original: It is VRRP that elects one router as the virtual router master, with the other routers acting as backups in case the virtual router master fails. HSRP is a Cisco-proprietary protocol. IRDP uses ICMP messages to allow IPv4 hosts to locate routers that provide IPv4 connectivity to other (nonlocal) IP networks. HSRP selects active and standby routers to provide gateway services to hosts on a LAN.

explain.s: HSRP elects an **active** and a **standby** router to share one gateway for the LAN.
x: The *master/backup* terminology is VRRP's.
ICMP router discovery is IRDP.
HSRP is Cisco-proprietary, not an open standard.

questions.question: Open the PT Activity. Perform the tasks in the activity instructions and then answer the question.

stem.text: What is the keyword that is displayed on www.netacad.com?

questions.original: In order for the host to receive the address of the DNS server, the host must use stateless DHCPv6. The router is configured with the correct DHCPv6 pool, but is missing the command ipv6 nd other-config-flag that signals to the host that it should use DHCPv6 to get additional address information. This command should be added to the interface Gigabit0/0 configuration on the router.

explain.s: The host needs the DNS server address, so it must use **stateless DHCPv6**. The router's pool is fine, but its LAN interface is missing the O flag. Once you add it, the host learns DNS and the page shows **Router**.

questions.question: Match each DHCP message type with its description. (Not all options are used.)
questions.original:
Place the options in the following order:
a client initiating a message to find a DHCP server - DHCPDISCOVER
a DHCP server responding to the initial request by a client - DHCPOFFER
the client accepting the IP address provided by the DHCP server - DHCPREQUEST
the DHCP server confirming that the lease has been accepted - DHCPACK

explain.s:
**DHCPDISCOVER** – the client looks for a server.
**DHCPOFFER** – the server's reply with a lease.
**DHCPREQUEST** – the client accepts the offered address.
**DHCPACK** – the server confirms the lease.

questions.question: Match the purpose with its DHCP message type. (Not all options are used.)
questions.original:
DHCPREQUEST
A message that is used to locate any available DHCP server on a network
DHCPOFFER
A message that is used to suggest a lease to a client
DHCPDISCOVER
A message that is used to identify the explicit server and lease offer to accept
DHCPNAK
A message that is used to acknowledge that the lease is successful
DHCPACK
A message is used by a server to finalize a successful lease with a client

explain.s:
**DHCPDISCOVER** – locate any available server.
**DHCPOFFER** – suggest a lease to the client.
**DHCPREQUEST** – say which server and lease you're accepting.
**DHCPACK** – the server finalizes the lease.
(DHCPNAK means the lease is refused.)
explain.note: The original explanation for this question pairs the messages with the wrong descriptions. The pairs above are the correct ones.

questions.question: Match the DHCP message types to the order of the stateful DHCPv6 process when a client first connects to an IPv6 network. (Not all options are used.)

explain.s:
Stateful DHCPv6 when a client first joins:
1. **RS** (Router Solicitation) → 2. **RA** with M=1 → 3. **SOLICIT** (look for DHCPv6 servers) → 4. **ADVERTISE** → 5. **REQUEST** → 6. **REPLY**.

questions.question: Match the step number to the sequence of stages that occur during the HSRP failover process. (Not all options are used.)

rows: The standby router stops seeing hello messages from the forwarding router.
The standby router assumes the role of the forwarding router.
The new forwarding router assumes both the IP and MAC addresses of the virtual router.

questions.original: Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP) is a Cisco-proprietary protocol that is designed to allow for transparent failover of a first-hop IPv4 device.

explain.s:
HSRP failover:
1. The forwarding (active) router **fails**.
2. The standby router **stops seeing hello messages** from it.
3. The standby router **becomes the forwarding role**.
4. It takes over the **virtual IP and virtual MAC**, so hosts keep using the same gateway.

questions.question: Match the FHRP protocols to the appropriate description. (Not all options are used.)

rows: a Cisco proprietary FHRP that provides load sharing in addition to redundancy
a Cisco proprietary FHRP that provides redundancy through use of an active device and standby device
an open standard FHRP that provides redundancy through use of a virtual routers master and one or more backups

explain.s:
**HSRP** – Cisco, one active and one standby.
**VRRPv2** – open standard, IPv4 only, one master.
**VRRPv3** – open standard, IPv4 and IPv6.
**GLBP** – Cisco, IPv4 load balancing.
**GLBP for IPv6** – Cisco, IPv6 load balancing.
**IRDP** – legacy, ICMP-based.

questions.question: Match the DHCP message types to the order of the DHCPv4 process. (Not all options are used.)
questions.original: The broadcast DHCPDISCOVER message finds DHCPv4 servers on the network. When the DHCPv4 server receives a DHCPDISCOVER message, it reserves an available IPv4 address to lease to the client and sends the unicast DHCPOFFER message to the requesting client. When the client receives the DHCPOFFER from the server, it sends back a DHCPREQUEST. On receiving the DHCPREQUEST message the server replies with a unicast DHCPACK message. DHCPREPLY and DHCPINFORMATION-REQUEST are DHCPv6 messages.

explain.s: DHCPv4 order: **DHCPDISCOVER → DHCPOFFER → DHCPREQUEST → DHCPACK**. Options such as DHCPREPLY or INFORMATION-REQUEST are DHCPv6 messages and are distractors.

questions.question: The address pool of a DHCP server is configured with 192.168.234.0/27. The network administrator reserves 22 IP addresses for IP phones. How many IP addresses are left in the pool to be assigned to other hosts?
questions.original:
Calculate the maximum number of hosts available for the slash value and subtract the required static IP addresses required for the devices.
/24 = 254 hosts
/25 = 126 hosts
/26 = 62 hosts
/27 = 30 hosts
/28 = 14 hosts

explain.s: A /27 has 2^5 − 2 = **30** usable addresses. Take away 22 reserved: **30 − 22 = 8**.

questions.question: A company uses DHCP servers to dynamically assign IPv4 addresses to employee workstations. The address lease duration is set as 5 days. An employee returns to the office after an absence of one week. When the employee boots the workstation, it sends a message to obtain an IP address. Which Layer 2 and Layer 3 destination addresses will the message contain?

options.text: both MAC and IPv4 addresses of the DHCP server
FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF and IPv4 address of the DHCP server
MAC address of the DHCP server and 255.255.255.255

questions.original: When the lease of a dynamically assigned IPv4 address has expired, a workstation will send a DHCPDISCOVER message to start the process of obtaining a valid IP address. Because the workstation does not know the addresses of DHCP servers, it sends the message via broadcast, with destination addresses of FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF and 255.255.255.255.

explain.s: The lease expired, so the client starts again with **DHCPDISCOVER**. It knows no server, so it uses **FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF** and **255.255.255.255**.

questions.question: Which command will allow a network administrator to check the IP address that is assigned to a particular MAC address?

options.text: Router# show ip dhcp server statistics

questions.original: The show ip dhcp binding command will show the leases, including IP addresses, MAC addresses, lease expiration, type of lease, client ID, and user name.

explain.s: `show ip dhcp binding` lists every lease: **IP address ↔ client MAC address**, expiry time and type.

questions.question: What is the reason that an ISP commonly assigns a DHCP address to a wireless router in a SOHO environment?
questions.original: In a SOHO environment, a wireless router connects to the ISP via a DSL or cable modem. The IP address between the wireless router and ISP site is typically assigned by the ISP through DHCP. This method facilitates the IP addressing management in that IP addresses for clients are dynamically assigned so that if a client is dropped, the assigned IP address can be easily reassigned to another client.

explain.s: Handing out addresses with DHCP makes **IP address management easy** for the ISP: addresses are assigned and reclaimed automatically, with no per-customer static setup.

questions.question: What information can be verified through the show ip dhcp binding command?

options.text: the IPv4 addresses that are assigned to hosts by the DHCP server
that DHCPv4 discover messages are still being received by the DHCP server
the IPv4 addresses that have been excluded from the DHCPv4 pool
the number of IP addresses remaining in the DHCP pool

questions.original: The show ip dhcp binding command shows a list of IPv4 addresses and the MAC addresses of the hosts to which they are assigned. Using this information an administrator can determine which host interfaces have been assigned to specific hosts.

explain.s: `show ip dhcp binding` shows **which IPv4 addresses the server has leased** and to which MAC address.
x: Pool usage and remaining addresses are in `show ip dhcp pool`.
Excluded addresses are in the running configuration.

questions.question: What is the result of a network technician issuing the command ip dhcp excluded-address 10.0.15.1 10.0.15.15 on a Cisco router?

options.text: The Cisco router will exclude only the 10.0.15.1 and 10.0.15.15 IP addresses from being leased to DHCP clients.
The Cisco router will exclude 15 IP addresses from being leased to DHCP clients.
The Cisco router will automatically create a DHCP pool using a /28 mask.
The Cisco router will allow only the specified IP addresses to be leased to clients.

questions.original: The ip dhcp excluded-address command is followed by the first and the last addresses to be excluded from being leased to DHCP clients.

explain.s: `ip dhcp excluded-address 10.0.15.1 10.0.15.15` excludes the **whole range**, .1 through .15. That's **15 addresses**.

questions.question: Match the descriptions to the corresponding DHCPv6 server type. (Not all options are used.)

explain.s:
**Stateless DHCPv6 server** – gives *only* extra settings, such as DNS and domain name. The host makes its own address with SLAAC. RA: M=0, O=1.
**Stateful DHCPv6 server** – gives the **address** and keeps track of who has which. RA: M=1.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Based on the output that is shown, what kind of IPv6 addressing is being configured?
questions.original: Stateful DHCPv6 pools are configured with address prefixes for hosts via the address command, whereas stateless DHCPv6 pools typically only contain information such as DNS server addresses and the domain name. RA messages that are sent from routers that are configured as stateful DHCPv6 servers have the M flag set to 1 with the command ipv6 nd managed-config-flag, whereas stateless DHCPv6 servers are indicated by setting the O flag to 1 with the ipv6 nd other-config-flag command.

explain.s: The pool contains only **DNS and domain name** information (no address prefix), and the interface has the O flag set. That's **stateless DHCPv6**.
x: Stateful DHCPv6 would use an `address prefix` line in the pool and `ipv6 nd managed-config-flag`.

questions.question: Which FHRP implementation is a Cisco-proprietary protocol that suppports IPv6 load balancing?

explain.s: **GLBP for IPv6** is Cisco-proprietary and load-balances **IPv6** traffic across several gateways.

questions.question: Which set of commands will configure a router as a DHCP server that will assign IPv4 addresses to the 192.168.100.0/23 LAN while reserving the first 10 and the last addresses for static assignment?

options.text:
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.1 192.168.100.9
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.101.254
ip dhcp pool LAN-POOL-100
ip network 192.168.100.0 255.255.254.0
ip default-gateway 192.168.100.1

dhcp pool LAN-POOL-100
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.1 192.168.100.9
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.254
network 192.168.100.0 255.255.254.0
default-router 192.168.101.1

ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.1 192.168.100.10
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.254
ip dhcp pool LAN-POOL-100
network 192.168.100.0 255.255.255.0
ip default-gateway 192.168.100.1

ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.1 192.168.100.10
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.101.254
ip dhcp pool LAN-POOL-100
network 192.168.100.0 255.255.254.0
default-router 192.168.100.1

questions.original: The /23 prefix is equivalent to a network mask of 255.255.254.0. The network usable IPv4 address range is 192.168.100.1 to 192.168.101.254 inclusive. The commands dhcp pool, ip default-gateway, and ip network are not valid DHCP configuration commands.

explain.s: /23 = mask **255.255.254.0**, so usable addresses run from 192.168.100.1 to **192.168.101.254**. Exclude .100.1–.100.10 (the first 10) and the last address (101.254), then build the pool with `network` and `default-router`.
x: `dhcp pool`, `ip network` and `ip default-gateway` aren't valid DHCP pool commands.

questions.question: What is a result when the DHCP servers are not operational in a network?

options.text: Workstations are assigned with the IP address 127.0.0.1.
Workstations are assigned with IP addresses in the 10.0.0.0/8 network.
Workstations are assigned with IP addresses in the 169.254.0.0/16 network.
Workstations are assigned with the IP address 0.0.0.0.

questions.original: When workstations are configured with obtaining IP address automatically but DHCP servers are not available to respond to the requests, a workstation can assign itself an IP addresses from the 169.254.0.0/16 network.

explain.s: If no DHCP server answers, hosts give themselves an **APIPA** address in **169.254.0.0/16**. They can only talk to other APIPA hosts on the same link.

questions.question: A company uses the method SLAAC to configure IPv6 addresses for the workstations of the employees. A network administrator configured the IPv6 address on the LAN interface of the router. The interface status is UP. However, the workstations on the LAN segment did not obtain the correct prefix and prefix length. What else should be configured on the router that is attached to the LAN segment for the workstations to obtain the information?​
questions.original: A PC that is configured to use the SLAAC method obtains the IPv6 prefix and prefix length from a router. When the PC boots, it sends an RS message to inform the routers that it needs the information. A router sends an RA message that includes the required information. For a router to be able to send RA messages, it must be enabled as an IPv6 router by the unicast ipv6-routing command in global configuration mode. The other options are not used to enable IPv6 routing on a router.

explain.s: A router sends Router Advertisements, which carry the prefix and prefix length that SLAAC needs, only after IPv6 routing is turned on. The missing command is `ipv6 unicast-routing`.
x: `ipv6 dhcp pool` is for DHCPv6, not SLAAC.
`ipv6 enable` only creates a link-local address.
The O flag is for stateless DHCPv6 extras.

questions.question: Which FHRP implementation is a nonproprietary protocol which relies on ICMP to provide IPv4 redundancy?

explain.s: **IRDP** (ICMP Router Discovery Protocol) is a legacy, nonproprietary method that uses **ICMP** messages to let hosts find gateways.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. PC-A is unable to receive an IPv6 address from the stateful DHCPv6 server. What is the problem?

options.text: The ipv6 dhcp relay command should be applied to interface Gig0/0.
The ipv6 nd managed-config-flag should be applied to interface Gig0/1.
The ipv6 dhcp relay command should use the link-local address of the DHCP server.
The ipv6 nd managed-config-flag command should be ipv6 nd other-config-flag .

questions.original: The ipv6 dhcp relay command must be applied to the interface where the clients are located. The ipv6 dhcp relay command can use either the link-local or global unicast address of the DHCPv6 server, or even a multicast address. The ipv6 nd managed-config-flag indicates to the clients that they should use stateful DHCPv6 and is also applied to the interface where the clients are located.

explain.s: The relay has to sit on the interface **where the clients are**, which is **Gig0/0**. There it can catch the clients' multicast SOLICIT messages and forward them to the server.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is configuring a router as a DHCPv6 server. The administrator issues a show ipv6 dhcp pool command to verify the configuration. Which statement explains the reason that the number of active clients is 0?

options.text: The default gateway address is not provided in the pool.
No clients have communicated with the DHCPv6 server yet.
The IPv6 DHCP pool configuration has no IPv6 address range specified.
The state is not maintained by the DHCPv6 server under stateless DHCPv6 operation.

questions.original: Under the stateless DHCPv6 configuration, indicated by the command ipv6 nd other-config-flag, the DHCPv6 server does not maintain the state information, because client IPv6 addresses are not managed by the DHCP server. Because the clients will configure their IPv6 addresses by combining the prefix/prefix-length and a self-generated interface ID, the ipv6 dhcp pool configuration does not need to specify the valid IPv6 address range. And because clients will use the link-local address of the router interface as the default gateway address, the default gateway address is not necessary.

explain.s: In **stateless DHCPv6** the server doesn't hand out addresses, so it has nothing to track. The *active clients* count therefore stays **0**, which is normal.

questions.question: Which FHRP implementation is Cisco-proprietary and permits only one router in a group to forward IPv6 packets?
